reasoning: I checked the WebSocket catch, protocol decoder, project-message handler, Monitor bus, and Reporter. The path is real: any PIN-admitted socket can repeatedly send malformed frames before the editor gate, and an editor—including one that claimed the role through `takeover`—can trigger synchronous `loadProject` filesystem or validation failures whose raw messages are returned by the outer catch; there is no per-socket response or Monitor-event rate limit. The Reporter does deduplicate identical errors into one queued record with an increasing count, so the finding overstates queue-entry multiplication, and decode validation is flattened into a single-line message rather than returning a raw multiline ZodError; however, every occurrence still emits an error frame, broadcasts a Monitor event, invokes `Reporter.observe`, increments the report count, and upserts the queue, while handler failures can expose filesystem paths or validation details. Those partial mitigations do not handle the plausible disclosure and amplification path, so the finding survives.
counter_evidence: Partial mitigation only: `apps/server/src/telemetry/reporter.ts:65-87` deduplicates repeated errors by key, and `apps/server/src/ws-protocol.ts:52-55` formats decode failures into one line. Neither redacts handler exceptions nor rate-limits `apps/server/src/main.ts:510-517`; `apps/server/src/handlers/projects.ts:33-34` lets `loadProject` filesystem/schema exceptions reach that catch.
